doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Leaving for Los Angeles in 1945 and finishing high school there
summary: He and Addison went to California for a supposed two weeks, stayed, finished high school at Thomas Jefferson and rented rooms.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Anything else we could talk about before we leave Phoenix and talk about your first trip to California?

No, we were waiting to get some jobs outside of Arizona, but they never came, so my brother and I decided to go to California. That’s when that part of our life started. We went to California one summer. We had told our mother we were going on vacation for two weeks, and that’s what we thought it would be. But when we got there, there was so much going on. There’s no way we could go back to Phoenix.
My brother went on the train because he had the bass, and he had it in a big wooden case. I went by car with another guy. We got to Central Avenue, and it was really jumping.
Do you remember the day that you got there?
No, I don’t remember. We would’ve gone a year earlier, but they had the Zoot Suit Riots.
That would’ve been the summer of ’44?
So, you went in the summer of ’45.

Yeah, that sounds like it. Everything was so happening, we couldn’t go back, so we just stayed there and managed to survive while you could still get a job because a lot of guys were in the army. We would get jobs playing, [and] if we didn’t get jobs playing, we’d get jobs doing manual labor. We finished our last year of high school at Thomas Jefferson. I remember my mother said if that’s what you wanna do, but just finish high school at least. So, I promised her I would do that, and we did it. Funny thing was that the school administration thought we were staying over there with our parents, but we were just staying by ourselves, so we would write our own excuses [laughs].
Where were you living in Los Angeles?

We would rent rooms. People would have a spare furnished room. We managed to keep that together. I remember when Charlie Parker came out there with Dizzy Gillespie. He stayed over in our place ‘cause he was a nomad.
